op.V1.question: How to reshape the rhythm
op.syncopate.hint: Notes on a beat start half a beat early and are held into the beat.
op.dotted.hint: Pairs of notes a quarter, an eighth or a 16th apart become long–short.
op.halfTime.hint: Every note twice as long, and twice as far from the start of the selection.
op.doubleTime.hint: Every note half as long, and half as far from the start of the selection.
op.later1.hint: Every note starts an eighth later; lengths stay.
op.later2.hint: Every note starts a quarter later; lengths stay.
op.later3.hint: Every note starts three eighths later; lengths stay.
op.V13.question: How long the notes sound
op.short.hint: Each note sounds for about a quarter of the time to the next one; pitches and onsets stay.
op.detached.hint: Each note sounds for about half of the time to the next one; pitches and onsets stay.
op.connected.hint: Each note holds until the next one starts; pitches and onsets stay.
op.V7.question: How many notes and rests there are
op.repeat8.hint: Each note a quarter or longer is played as repeated eighths at its pitch.
op.repeat16.hint: Each note an eighth or longer is played as repeated sixteenths at its pitch.
op.mergeRepeats.hint: Notes repeated at one pitch, one straight after the other, become one longer note.
op.moreAir.hint: An eighth's rest before each note that follows straight on; every note starts where it did.
op.fillRests.hint: Each note is held to the next one, so the rests go.
op.V8.question: Which notes are accented
op.accentOnBeat.hint: Notes on a beat play louder, the others softer; pitches and timing stay.
op.accentOffBeat.hint: Notes between the beats play louder, the others softer.
op.accentEveryThird.hint: Every third onset, from the first, plays louder, so the accents cut across the meter.
op.accentDownbeat.hint: Only notes that start a bar play louder.
op.V11.question: What is added between the melody notes
op.passing.hint: The scale notes between two melody notes a third to a fifth apart, in the second half of the first.
op.upperNeighbour.hint: The scale step above each melody note, in its second half, before the next note.
op.lowerNeighbour.hint: The scale step below each melody note, in its second half, before the next note.
op.V3.question: How the chords are voiced and where the notes sit
op.rootPosition.hint: Each chord with its root in the bass; the chord's notes stay, some move an octave.
op.firstInversion.hint: Each chord with its third in the bass.
op.secondInversion.hint: Each chord with its fifth in the bass.
op.closeVoicing.hint: The notes over each chord's bass gathered into the octave above it.
op.openVoicing.hint: The second-highest note of each chord an octave lower, so the chord spreads wider.
op.octaveUp.hint: Every note of the step an octave higher; pitch classes and rhythm stay.
op.octaveDown.hint: Every note of the step an octave lower; pitch classes and rhythm stay.
op.otherHand.hint: The highest left-hand note of each chord moves to the right hand.
op.V6.question: How much simpler
op.simplify1.hint: The inner voices are left out: only the melody and the bass stay.
op.simplify2.hint: Also one root per chord in the bass.
op.simplify3.hint: Also every note on the eighth grid, and melody leaps over an octave folded.
op.V14.question: How the long notes are ornamented
op.graceAbove.hint: The note a step above for a 32nd on the note's beat, then the note held.
op.graceBelow.hint: The note a step below for a 32nd on the note's beat, then the note held.
op.mordent.hint: The note, the note above and the note again in 32nds, then the note held.
op.lowerMordent.hint: The note, the note below and the note again in 32nds, then the note held.
op.turn.hint: The note above, the note, the note below in 32nds, then the note held.
op.trill.hint: The note and the note above in turn for half the note, then the note held.
op.V12.question: What the bass plays under each chord
op.rootsOnly.hint: The root of each chord, held for the chord.
op.rootAndFifth.hint: The root for the first half of each chord, then the fifth above it.
op.octaves.hint: The root and the root an octave away, one per beat.
op.walk.hint: The root, then a scale step on each beat towards the next chord's root.
op.pedal.hint: The key's tonic under every chord, struck again in each bar.
op.V15.question: Which chords go under the melody
op.relative.hint: Each major chord becomes its relative minor and each minor chord its relative major; the melody stays.
op.parallel.hint: Each major chord becomes minor on the same root, and each minor chord major; the melody stays.
op.V2.question: How the accompaniment plays its notes
op.heldChord.hint: Each bar's accompaniment notes, struck together once and held to the end of the bar.
op.repeatedChord.hint: Each bar's accompaniment notes, struck together on every eighth.
op.arpeggioUp.hint: One accompaniment note per 16th, from the lowest to the highest, then again.
op.arpeggioDown.hint: One accompaniment note per 16th, from the highest to the lowest, then again.
op.upDown.hint: One accompaniment note per triplet eighth, up to the highest and back down.
op.alberti.hint: Lowest, highest, middle, highest, one per 16th. Needs three different notes in each bar.
op.V4.question: Where the copies go
op.stepHigher.hint: A copy of the motif follows straight after, one scale step higher.
op.stepLower.hint: A copy of the motif follows straight after, one scale step lower.
op.climbing.hint: Three copies follow, each one scale step higher than the one before.
op.thirdLower.hint: A copy of the motif follows straight after, two scale steps lower.
op.V9.question: How the steps of the melody change
op.wider.hint: Each step of the melody grows by a scale step; the rhythm and the contour stay.
op.muchWider.hint: Each step of the melody grows by two scale steps; the rhythm and the contour stay.
op.narrower.hint: Each step of the melody shrinks by a scale step; the rhythm and the contour stay.
op.V10.question: How the melody turns
op.upsideDown.hint: The melody moves the other way from its first note, in scale steps of the key.
op.upsideDownExact.hint: The melody moves the other way from its first note, by the same number of semitones.

settings.photoPagesHint: Add a piece from photos: photograph the pages in a row with the iPad's camera, or pick photos in Photos or Files. They become one PDF piece on this iPad. Recognise notes then sends one page at a time, shows each page as it is done, and says which pages to photograph again.

settings.pieces: Several pieces in a score or recording
settings.piecesHint: When a score or a concert recording holds several pieces, the Contents propose where each one begins (a pause alone is not a boundary). Remove, move or add a boundary, name each piece and confirm; then make each a piece of its own in the library, in one playlist. A recording's pieces get bars and a tempo of their own. The file itself is not cut.
settings.liveTempoHint: In a recording, the beats and bars are found again after each pause and each jump in tempo, so a concert of several pieces keeps its bars. The metre and tempo of a score, when there is one, are a hint for the recording, not a rule.
settings.piecesPdfHint: When a PDF or photographed pages hold several pieces, “Pieces in this file” in the Contents makes each piece's pages a piece of its own in the library, in one playlist. Start from the page bookmarks or list the pages by hand. The file itself is not cut.

settings.harmony: Reference: chords, scales and the harmony explorer
settings.harmonyHint: Circle opens the Reference with three sections. Keys: the circle of fifths with the number of sharps or flats round it, each key a shade darker the more it has. Chords and scales: choose what sounds, a chord or a scale from any note, then how it sounds: the inversion, close or open, together, up, down or broken, once or in a loop. Explorer: build a progression from a key's chords and hear it in a texture. Nothing is written into the piece.

tempo.noScore: Add a version from a score of the piece first: its metre and tempo are the hint.
tempo.liveHow: The beat is found again after each pause and each jump in tempo; the pieces of the piece layer move along with the recording. A score's metre and tempo are a hint, never a rule.
tempo.sectionsFound: Sections: {0}. Bars of {1}, a quarter at about {2}.
tempo.hintNoFit: The score's {0} did not fit: the recording reads {1}.
settings.readingMarks: For reading: rit., fermatas and dynamics
settings.readingMarksHint: A recording's score for reading also shows how it was played where it matters: a dynamic where the playing gets markedly louder or softer, rit. and accel. where it slows down or speeds up a lot, and a fermata over a chord held far longer than the beats around it. Accents, crescendos, slurs and pedal stay in As played. All of it is worked out from the recording.
score.readingMarks: The dynamics, rit., accel. and fermatas that matter are worked out from the recording: how loud the bars were played and where the playing slowed, sped up or held.
settings.playheadsHint: The black playhead is the place in the piece, the blue one the place inside the selection. One Play button, in the pill: blue while the selection plays, black once playback goes on through the piece. Loop goes to the selection's start and repeats it; a click on a beat outside the selection turns Loop off. A selection goes by beats and changes only by its handles; a click places a playhead and never changes it; ✕ or Escape removes it. The bar chooses what the mouse does: Navigate, Select, Edit notes or Pen (keys H, S, E, P).

settings.metersHint: In a recording's Check, says where its bars read better in 5/8, 7/8, 9/8, 5/4 or 12/8 than in the signature found, worked out from where the bass falls. Only a preview: the bars stay as they are and nothing is saved.
tempo.oddMetersNone: No stretch reads better in 5/8, 7/8, 9/8, 5/4 or 12/8.
tempo.oddMetersHow: A preview worked out from where the bass falls, eight bars at a time: the bars stay as they are and nothing is saved.

settings.assistantRepairs: Repairs for the bars to check (preview)
settings.assistantRepairsHint: In Check, Repair under a flagged bar offers ways to correct it that the app works out from the flag's reason, with no AI and on this device: a repeated note removed, three notes read as a triplet, a note one step too long shortened. The bar shows the correction above it; hear it, then Accept to add it to My corrections, or Dismiss. The flag stays until you say Looks right.
settings.assistantHint: Ask opens the assistant in Insights: it answers about the selection or the whole piece with an AI model, and every answer cites the facts the app found, each with its place in the score. Before the first question it shows exactly what is sent; nothing is sent until you agree and the assistant is switched on for your account.
settings.assistantActionsHint: With Assistant conversation on: ask the assistant to change the selected bars, such as removing a stray note, moving a note, changing its pitch or length, tying two notes, repairing a flagged bar or trying a variant. It chooses one of the app's operations; the app makes the notes and shows them as a draft over the bars. Hear it, then Accept to add it to My corrections, or Cancel. The assistant never writes notes itself.
settings.assistantContext: Assistant at the selection, and kept conversations (preview)
settings.assistantContextHint: With Assistant conversation on: Ask on a selection opens a small assistant right there for one question, which keeps nothing; Add to context moves its answer into the assistant's conversation about the piece. The assistant's conversations are kept on this device, by piece, never in the project file, and its list goes back to an earlier one.
settings.sourcesHint: The switch of every view of the piece above the score and the Sources sheet by originals and notes: another PDF, recognise a recording, recognise again, remove an original and keep its notes, and Make working. Your own files are never changed.
settings.musicalIdeas: Ideas by what they are in the music (preview)
settings.musicalIdeasHint: In Piece DNA, the ideas are the theme, the contrasting section, a sequence, the motif heard most often and the highest point, each only where the app finds it in the notes. Each card says in one line why it was chosen, from what the app measured: the closes, the sections, the repeats, notes per beat, the highest note and the key. Off, the ideas are the phrase openings heard most often, as before.

settings.assistantVariantsHint: In phrase focus, What if… under the card makes variants of the phrase with the app's own operations, with no AI and on this device: from the original or from the variant shown. Each is heard as the plum ossia over the phrase and compared with the original; Keep puts it in the card's header (the last four), and Take into work puts it into your working notes in place of the phrase. The original is not changed, and Undo or the assembly journal takes it back.
